summary: Prepare for DevOps and platform roles: CI/CD, infrastructure as code, containers and Kubernetes, observability and incident response.

topics.title: CI/CD pipelines
topics.why: Almost every DevOps interview asks how you ship changes safely.

topics.title: Infrastructure as code
topics.why: Expect questions on state, drift and team workflows.
points: Drift and how to handle it

topics.title: Containers and Kubernetes
topics.why: Many roles run workloads on Kubernetes.
points: Images, registries and small secure images

topics.title: Observability
topics.why: You'll be asked how you'd know something is wrong.
points: Service level objectives and error budgets

topics.title: Incident response
topics.why: A good incident story is one of the strongest answers you can give.

exercises.title: Build a pipeline
exercises.goal: Have a real pipeline to describe.
steps: Create a small app in your code editor with one test.
Add a CI pipeline that tests and builds a container image.
Add a deploy step to a local cluster (kind or minikube) or a mock.
Record a walkthrough of the pipeline and what you'd improve.

exercises.title: Break and fix a deployment
exercises.goal: Practise an incident story end to end.
steps: Deploy the app to a local Kubernetes cluster.
Introduce a fault (a bad image tag, a failing health check).
Find it using kubectl and logs, fix it, and write a short post-incident note.
Record yourself telling the story: detection, steps, fix, prevention.

exercises.title: Infrastructure as code with review
steps: Write Terraform for a small resource (a local or sandbox provider).
Show plan output and how a reviewer would read it.
Record a short explanation of how you'd apply it across environments.

practice.title: DevOps Engineer
practice.summary: Practice interview for a DevOps engineer: pipelines, infrastructure as code, Kubernetes and reliability.

anchors.3: Built or improved a pipeline with a measurable effect.
anchors.5: Designed a pipeline with tests, security checks, rollout and rollback, with results.

competencies.name: Infrastructure as code
competencies.description: Manages infrastructure with code and review.

anchors.3: Manages infrastructure as code with reviews.
anchors.5: Structures code for teams and environments, handling state and drift.

anchors.3: Describes deploying and running a service on Kubernetes.
anchors.5: Describes tuning resources, scaling and safe rollouts with results.

competencies.name: Reliability and incidents
competencies.description: Keeps services healthy and learns from incidents.

anchors.3: Walks through an incident they handled.
anchors.5: Walks through an incident end to end, including communication and prevention.

questions.text: Tell me about a pipeline you built or improved. What did you change, and what difference did it make?
Tell me about a time you managed infrastructure with code. How did you keep changes safe?
Imagine a deployment to Kubernetes keeps restarting. How would you find out why?
Tell me about an incident you were part of. What did you do, and what changed afterwards?
How would you decide what to alert on for a new service?

practice.company_facts: This is a practice interview. There is no real employer: questions about pay, hours or the team can't be answered here.

settings.next_steps: Your coaching feedback appears as soon as the interview ends.
